label: Treatment recap
subject: Good seeing you, Stedi
preheader: A quick recap of what we talked about.
body:
Hi Stedi,

Thank you for coming in. We covered a lot at the visit, so here is the short version of what we discussed about your crown.

A crown is a custom-made cover that fits over a tooth that is cracked, heavily filled, or worn down, and restores its full shape and strength. It holds the tooth together so you can chew with confidence, and it is shaded to blend in with the teeth around it.

The next step is simply picking a time that works for you. Reply to this email or call us at (918) 555-0100.

If anything was unclear, or a question came to you on the drive home, send it my way. That is what I am here for.

label: What to expect
subject: What the appointment is actually like
preheader: A walk-through, so there are no surprises.
body:
Hi Stedi,

The unknown is usually the hardest part, so here is what your appointment is actually like.

A crown usually takes two visits a couple of weeks apart, and you wear a temporary crown in between. Plan on about an hour to an hour and a half for the first appointment.

You will be fully numb for the procedure, and we check in with you throughout.

Afterward: Mild gum tenderness and sensitivity to temperature for a few days is normal.

That is really it. If knowing more would help, ask me anything. Reply to this email or call us at (918) 555-0100.

label: Common questions
subject: Two questions we hear all the time
preheader: Answers from the Roland Family Dental team.
body:
Hi Stedi,

When patients are deciding on the crown, these are two questions we hear most often.

Why a crown instead of a bigger filling?
Once a tooth has lost a lot of its structure, a filling has nothing solid to hold onto and the tooth can split. A crown wraps the tooth and holds it together.

How long do crowns last?
Many crowns last ten years or more. Home care, regular cleanings, and protecting against grinding make the biggest difference.

Have a different question? Reply and ask. And when you are ready, reply to this email or call us at (918) 555-0100.

label: What waiting means
subject: An honest word about timing
preheader: What tends to happen when treatment waits.
body:
Hi Stedi,

I do not want to pressure you, and I also would not be doing my job if I did not share the honest picture on timing for your crown.

A tooth that needs a crown is a tooth under stress. The longer it goes unprotected, the higher the chance it cracks further or the nerve becomes involved, and both of those mean more treatment than a crown alone.

That is why we would rather see you sooner than later. If cost, time, or nerves are in the way, let me help with that part. Reply here or call (918) 555-0100.
